title: Patience in the Process
subtitle: Thirteen years, twenty-five years. And work the whole time.
objectives: Give examples of long waits in scripture
Explain that patience is active, not passive
Explain the farmer image in James 5

cards.title: Patience is not doing nothing
cards.text: Every long wait in scripture is full of work. Joseph ran a household and then a prison while he waited thirteen years.

cards.title: Real waits, with real numbers
cards.text: Abstract patience is forgettable. Measured patience is not.
points: **Joseph:** sold at seventeen, before Pharaoh at thirty.
**Thirteen years**, including prison for something he did not do.
**Abraham:** promised a son at seventy-five, Isaac born at a hundred.
**Twenty-five years** between the promise and the child.

cards.title: Four people who waited, and how long they waited
cards.text: Tap each one. The last two buttons are the point.

question.explain: Seventeen to thirty. Genesis 37 and 41 give both ages.

cards.title: The farmer, chosen on purpose
cards.text: Of all the images available, the letter picks the one that involves labour.
points: **James 5:7:** be patient, like a farmer waiting for the rain.
**A farmer is not idle while waiting.**
**He planted. He weeds. He watches the sky.**
**Nothing visible happens for weeks.** He keeps going anyway.

question.text: Why is a farmer the right image for patience?
question.explain: Patience that is work, not waiting around.

cards.title: Romans 5:3-4
cards.text: The order in the verse matters.
points: **Suffering produces endurance.**
**Endurance produces character.**
**Character produces hope.**
**Each one is made by the one before it.** None can be skipped.

cards.title: The plateau is the part that decides it
cards.text: Everyone improves fast at first. Then the numbers stop moving.
points: **Weeks of work with no visible change.**
**That is where most people quit.**
**The adaptation is happening** where you cannot see it.
**The plateau is not failure.** It is the middle.

cards.title: Your height is on its own schedule
cards.text: Nothing you do this week will change it, and it is changing anyway.
points: **Growth plates close in their own time.**
**You cannot hurry it and cannot stop it.**
**Meanwhile the things you can change** respond to months of work.
**Spend the wait on those.**

question.text: Patience in scripture means waiting without doing anything.
question.explain: Joseph ran a household and then a prison for the whole thirteen years.

cards.title: Months from now
cards.alt: A single green rice seedling standing above the still water of a flooded paddy at dawn
cards.text: The farmer in James 5 is not waiting around. He planted this and he weeds it.

cards.title: A restoration is measured in years
cards.text: Anyone who has rebuilt something knows the shape of this.
points: **Months with the car in pieces** and nothing to show.
**Every part cleaned, labelled, waiting.**
**The first time it starts** is one afternoon.
**Everything before it was the project.**

cards.title: What to remember
points: Joseph waited thirteen years; Abraham twenty-five.
Patience is active. Joseph ran a household and a prison.
James 5:7 uses a farmer because a farmer works while waiting.
Romans 5: suffering, endurance, character, hope. In that order.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 4 Devotion. Patience is given numbers, because abstract patience is forgettable and thirteen years is not. Both of the key figures' ages come straight from the text and are checkable, which matters for a learner who should be building the habit of asking where a claim comes from. The week's central correction is that patience is active: Joseph was running a household and then a prison for the whole thirteen years, which is a very different picture from waiting around. James 5's farmer is used for exactly that reason. The boxing lens names the plateau, which is the form this virtue will actually take for him this year.
discussion: Ask how long Joseph and Abraham waited.
Ask what Joseph was doing during those years.
Ask why James chose a farmer.
Ask what a plateau means in training.
extension: Have him pick one thing to work at for eight weeks and record it weekly.
Have him find the two verses that give Joseph's ages.
misconceptions: "Patience means waiting passively." Every example in the text is working.
"A plateau means it is not working." It is the middle of it working.
